originalTitle: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy
title: Friends Across the Sea: Talking About People Moving Home
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends from across Africa! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you a story about two countries far away. Sometimes, even big countries have things they need to talk about, just like you and your friends might need to chat about who plays with which toy! Today, we're going to learn about a conversation happening between a country called the United Kingdom, or the UK for short, and another country called Eritrea. Let's find out what's going on!

Meet Our Friends, UK and Eritrea!

Imagine our world as a giant playground. On this playground, there are many different areas, and each area is a country! Today, we are looking at two special areas. The United Kingdom is a country in Europe. It's an island, which means it has water all around it, like a big boat floating in the ocean. People there speak English, and they have a Queen (or King) and a government that helps run things. **Did you know?** The UK is famous for its red buses and big clocks called Big Ben! Eritrea is a beautiful country right here in Africa! It's on the eastern side, by the Red Sea. People in Eritrea speak different languages, like Tigrinya and Arabic, and it's known for its lovely coastlines and old cities. **Did you know?** Eritrea has many different types of animals, and its capital city, Asmara, has amazing old buildings! So, these two countries are far apart, but they often talk and interact with each other.

What is a "Migrant"? (A Big Word Made Simple!)

Sometimes, people decide to move from one country to another. They pack their bags, say goodbye to their homes, and go to live in a new place. These people are called "migrants." Why do people move? Well, there are many reasons! Some people move to find new jobs, like when a parent gets a special job in a different city. Others move to go to a good school or university, to learn new things. Sometimes, people move to be with their family members who live far away. And sadly, sometimes people move because their home country is not safe, and they need to find a new, peaceful place to live. **Did you know?** People have been moving between countries for thousands of years! It's part of human history. When people move to a new country, they often need special permission to live and work there. It's a bit like needing a special ticket to ride a big bus to another town.

Coming Home: The "Return Policy"

Now, imagine you're visiting a friend's house. You play games, have snacks, and have a wonderful time. But then, when it gets late, your parents tell you it's time to go home. You have to "return" to your own house. Countries sometimes have rules, like big parents, about people who have moved there. These rules are called a "return policy." It means that if someone has come to live in their country, but they don't have the right papers, or if it's time for them to go back, the country might ask them to "return" to their home country. The UK has a "return policy." It means that sometimes, they ask people who are living in the UK to go back to their home country if they don't have the right permission to stay. **Did you know?** Many countries have rules about who can live there, just like your house has rules about who can come inside!

The Big Talk: UK and Eritrea

So, here's the conversation between the UK and Eritrea. The UK wants some people who came from Eritrea and are living in the UK to return to Eritrea. But for these people to go back home safely, Eritrea needs to help. It's like if your friend wants to return a toy to your house, but you need to open the door for them. Eritrea needs to open the door and help its citizens return. Right now, the UK thinks that Eritrea is not helping enough. They believe Eritrea is "refusing to co-operate," which means not wanting to work together on this issue. **Did you know?** When countries work together, it's called "cooperation." It makes everyone's lives easier and better!

What Happens If Countries Don't Agree?

When countries don't agree, like when two friends can't decide what game to play, things can get a little tricky. The UK has a very important leader called the Home Secretary. She is like a head teacher for rules about people coming into and leaving the country. She has said that if Eritrea continues not to help, the UK might have to put in place "measures." What does that mean? "Measures" can be like saying "no" to some things. For example, it could mean making it harder for people from Eritrea to visit the UK, or stopping other kinds of help or cooperation between the two countries. It's like when you and your friend can't agree, and maybe you decide not to share your crayons for a little while until you can talk it out. The UK is saying they might "ban" some things, which means stopping them from happening. **Did you know?** Leaders from different countries often meet to talk and solve problems. This is called diplomacy, and it's a very important job!

Why Is It Important to Work Together?

It's always best when countries work together, just like it's best when friends play nicely. When countries cooperate, they can help each other with trade, education, health, and many other things. Finding solutions together means everyone can be happier and safer. When there are disagreements, it can make things difficult for people who want to travel, work, or study. We all hope that the UK and Eritrea can talk and find a way to work together, so that people can live peacefully and go where they need to go, with everyone's help. **Did you know?** Many African countries work together in groups like the African Union to help each other and solve problems on our continent!

What Happens Next?

So, what's next for the UK and Eritrea? We hope that the leaders of both countries will continue to talk. They will try to find a way for people to return home if they need to, in a way that is fair and safe for everyone. It's like when you have a little problem with a friend. You talk about it, you listen to each other, and you try to find a solution so you can be good friends again. We will keep watching to see how this story unfolds! That's all for today from your friendly news reporter. Remember to be kind to your friends, and always try to work things out by talking!
summary: The UK is asking Eritrea to help some Eritrean people return home from the UK, and if Eritrea doesn't cooperate, the UK might stop some things or make travel harder.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows how countries need to work together to help people move between places, and when they don't, it can cause problems for many people.

originalTitle: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
title: Kenya Helps Keep Everyone Safe from a Sickness
content:
Hello, Friends! Big News from Kenya!

Hello, everyone! It's your friendly reporter here, bringing you important news from our lovely country, Kenya. We have some news about a special sickness that doctors are working very hard to help with. Don't worry, everyone is doing their best to keep our friends and families safe and healthy.

What is This Sickness? It's Called Ebola

There is a sickness called Ebola. It's a bit of a big word, isn't it? Ebola is caused by tiny, tiny germs that we cannot see with our eyes. They are smaller than a speck of dust! These tiny germs can make people feel very, very sick. They might feel tired, have a fever, or their tummy might hurt a lot. It's not like a cold or the flu that most people get. It's a special kind of sickness. **Did you know?** Germs are everywhere! Most germs are good for us, but some can make us sick. That's why washing our hands is super important!

How Does Ebola Spread?

Now, you might be thinking, "Can I get Ebola from just playing with my friends?" No, not usually! Ebola is not like a cold where you can catch it from someone coughing or sneezing near you. Ebola spreads when you touch the body fluids of someone who is very, very sick with it. Body fluids mean things like sweat, pee, vomit, or even blood from a sick person. So, if you hug someone or share food, you usually won't get Ebola. It's different from those everyday sicknesses. It means you have to be very close and touch a sick person's fluids to get it. **Did you know?** Doctors and nurses wear special suits, gloves, and masks when they are helping people with Ebola. This keeps them safe from the tiny germs!

The First Friend Who Needed Help

A little while ago, a man came to Kenya. He had traveled from a country called DR Congo. DR Congo is a country not too far from Kenya, just like a long bus ride or airplane trip away. This man became very sick with Ebola. Our amazing doctors and nurses tried their very best to help him. Sadly, the man passed away. We are very sad for his family and friends.

Now, Another Friend Needs Help

After the first man got sick, our doctors and health workers checked everyone who was very close to him. They found that one of his family members also became sick with Ebola. This person lived with him. This is why it's super important for doctors to check people who live with or care for someone sick. Family members often live together and help each other. If they are not careful, it's easier for tiny germs to pass between them. Our doctors quickly found this family member and are giving them the best care right now. **Did you know?** Doctors call this "contact tracing." It's like finding all the friends a sick person played with to make sure everyone is safe and healthy!

What Are Our Doctors Doing?

Our brave doctors and nurses in Kenya are working very, very hard right now. They are taking wonderful care of the sick family member. They give them special medicine and make sure they are comfortable. They are also making sure that the sickness does not spread to more people in Kenya. They are checking on everyone who was near the sick family members. This helps to catch any sickness early before it can spread. They have special places called hospitals where sick people can get the best care and be away from others, so the germs don't spread.

How Can We All Stay Safe?

The best way to stay safe from all kinds of sicknesses, including Ebola, is to wash your hands! Wash your hands with soap and water for as long as it takes to sing "Happy Birthday" twice! That's how long you need to wash away germs. If you ever feel sick, tell an adult right away. Your parents, teachers, or guardians will know what to do to help you. Try not to touch your eyes, nose, or mouth too much, because germs can get into your body that way. Always listen to your grown-ups and follow their rules about staying healthy. **Did you know?** Washing your hands properly is like a superpower against germs! It washes them right down the drain!

Good News and Hope!

The good news is that doctors know a lot about Ebola now. They have special medicines that can help people get better when they are sick. There are even special shots, called vaccines, that can help stop people from getting sick with Ebola in the first place! Our amazing leaders and health workers in Kenya are doing everything they can to keep everyone in our country safe and sound. We can all help by listening to our grown-ups, keeping ourselves clean, and being kind. Let's all be kind and support those who are working hard to make everyone healthy! Hooray for our Kenyan heroes!
summary: Kenya has found a second person with the Ebola sickness, who is a family member of the first person, and doctors are working super hard to help them get better and keep everyone safe.
whyMatters: It's important because we want all our friends and family in Kenya to be healthy and safe from all kinds of sicknesses. Doctors are working super hard to make sure this sickness does not spread to more people, keeping our country safe for everyone to play and learn!
